sources.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory
sources.locator: The local fixed-order EFT construction is in §2.2.1–2.2.5, printed pp. 21–28, PDF pp. 21–28; the redundant-interaction and leading-EOM field-redefinition argument is in the §2.1 discussion, printed pp. 14–15, equations (21)–(26).

contents.name: §§2.2.1–2.2.5 and §3 opening: fixed-order local operators and engineering dimensions
contents.support: The EFT convention that a fixed low-energy order uses a finite set of local interactions with specified engineering dimensions and coefficients.

contents.name: §2.1, equations (21)–(26): integration by parts and leading-equation field redefinition
contents.support: At a single retained order, a term proportional to the leading variational equation is canceled by an identity-leading field redefinition; total derivatives are removed under the stated boundary convention.

contents.name: §2.1, equations (25)–(26): scalar derivative-operator reduction
contents.support: The toy scalar density used as the worked example of a derivative operator related to lower-derivative interactions. The worked item independently derives its displayed result from the local hypotheses and conventions.

sources.title: Matthias Neubert, Effective Field Theory and Heavy Quark Physics (2004 TASI Lectures)
sources.locator: Read §2, PDF pp. 5–17, including equations (2)–(12) on mode splitting, local operators, engineering dimensions and finite-order truncation, and equations (27)–(29) on leading-EOM operator redundancy.

contents.name: §2, equations (2)–(12): local operators, coefficient dimensions, and finite truncation
contents.support: The coefficient-dimension convention and the need to declare a fixed field content, symmetry allowance, dimension, and truncation order before discussing a finite operator set.

contents.name: §2, pp. 11–12: symmetry-allowed operator enumeration
contents.support: A basis is selected only after symmetries, dimension, field content, and algebraic relations have been fixed. The worked item independently derives its displayed result from the local hypotheses and conventions.

contents.name: §2, equations (27)–(29): leading-equation operator elimination
contents.support: The distinction between equation-of-motion reduction at a stated EFT order and an unrestricted assertion about off-shell correlators.

sources.title: Juan Carlos Criado and Manuel Pérez-Victoria, Field redefinitions in effective theories at higher orders
sources.locator: Read §2, PDF pp. 6–8, equations (2.2)–(2.8), on regulated change of variables, Jacobian, sources and LSZ; §3, PDF pp. 9–12, equations (3.1)–(3.8), on the first-order EOM rule and its higher-order limitation; §5.1, PDF pp. 17–19, equations (5.2)–(5.5), on order-by-order field redefinitions; and Appendix B, PDF pp. 33–34, equations (B.1)–(B.11), checking single versus multiple EOM insertions.

contents.name: §§3 and 5.1: first-order equation use and order-by-order redefinitions
contents.support: The EOM relation is valid as a first-order coefficient-space relation; at higher orders the actual invertible field redefinition generates additional terms that must be retained.

contents.name: §2 and Appendix B: Jacobian, transformed source, LSZ, and multiple insertions
contents.support: For local perturbative invertible redefinitions, the regulated generating functional remains equal when the Jacobian and source transformation are retained, and LSZ-normalized amplitudes agree for stable external particles with nonzero one-particle overlap; one EOM insertion vanishes on shell at linear order, while multiple insertions need not.

contents.name: Appendix B: first-order versus multiple equation insertions
contents.support: The example's boundary between first-order EOM reduction and higher-order corrections. The worked item independently derives its displayed result from the local hypotheses and conventions.

sources.title: Michel Brion, Introduction to actions of algebraic groups
sources.locator: Read Theorem 1.23 and the Reynolds-operator portion of Theorem 1.24 in full, printed pp. 8–9, PDF pp. 9–10, including the equivariant-surjection argument.

contents.name: Theorems 1.23–1.24: Reynolds projection and surjectivity on invariants
contents.support: The imported theorem's exact hypothesis and conclusion that an equivariant surjection of rational modules induces a surjection on invariant subspaces.

sources.title: Edward Witten, Notes On Supermanifolds And Integration
sources.locator: §3.1, equation (3.6), printed pp. 10–11; Step 3a passage review only

contents.name: Block Berezinian convention
contents.support: Context for the explicitly defined block formula; no analytic integration theorem is imported and the exact coordinate-change identity remains a supplied hypothesis.
